Your pDC cluster is split into Plasma cell, cDC1, pDC and cDC2 at low confidence. Cells in all three main call groups (Plasma cell, cDC1, pDC) carry the same pDC program (TCF4 95-97%, BLNK 99%, SPIB 74-79%, PLD4 84-88%) and lack B/plasma identity (CD79B, MS4A1, PAX5 <=1%; TNFRSF17 0%; PRDM1 <=6%; JCHAIN <=6%). cDC1-called cells also lack the cDC1 genes that mark C3 (XCR1 16%, BATF3 1%, CADM1 4%). These are cross-species misclassifications of pDC-like cells. Removing the immunoglobulin genes IGKC, IGHM and IGHD lowered Plasma calls only from 1,579 to 1,181, so they contribute but are not the main driver. The human pDC markers LILRA4, CLEC4C and IL3RA have no verified pig orthologue and are zero-filled; in a human control, zero-filling all pig-unmapped genes still left pDCs called pDC (95%).

Separates interstitial (C3) from alveolar macrophages, but misclassifies monocytes and monocyte-derived macrophages as cDC2, cDC or Neutrophil. In alveolar macrophages the 'M1 macrophage' share rises with EVLP time in every pig, but it does not track the classical inflammatory/interferon programme (see C1), so it should not be read as M1 polarization.

Your alveolar macrophages are split between Alveolar macrophage and M1 macrophage, separate branches in the model. Within every pig sampled later, the M1 share rises from T0H (19-51% per pig) to T10H (60-77%; T8H, a single specimen, 64%); descriptive, post hoc, no statistical test. This does not reflect classical M1 activation: in your pseudobulk results for this cluster the interferon-gamma, TNF-alpha/NF-kB and inflammatory-response Hallmark sets are higher at T4H than at T10H, and CXCL10, GBP1, IRF1, STAT1 and TNF are lower at T10H than at T0H. Within each specimen (23/23), M1-called cells instead show higher CTSL, CTSB, ARG1, MAFB, S100A8, VIM and GPNMB and lower C1QA/B/C and FCN2 than Alveolar-called cells. Read 'M1 macrophage' as the model's label for this shifted state, not as M1 polarization; the M1/M2 dichotomy is itself a simplification (Murray et al., Immunity 2014, PMID 25035950).

Your inflammatory monocytes are split into cDC2, CD14 monocyte and Neutrophil. Cells called Neutrophil or cDC2 express monocyte genes (CD14 78-93%, VCAN 73-82%) and lack the neutrophil granule genes (MMP8 0%, LTF <=12%) and the DC genes (FCER1A <=1%, ZBTB46 <=5%, IRF4 <=5%). This is the same kind of cross-species misclassification as the pDCs called plasma cells in the DC subset.
